blogs.title: The Normal MRI Trap: Diagnosing Neuro-Behçet's Without Parenchymal Lesions
blogs.description: Early acute neuro-Behçet's disease can present with aseptic meningitis and a completely normal brain MRI. This post discusses the limitations of neuroimaging in the early inflammatory phase and emphasizes the critical role of CSF analysis (lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein) when clinical suspicion remains high despite negative imaging.

blogs.title: Hiccups, Rhabdo, and Hyponatremia: Recognizing the Silent Killer in CNS Inflammation
blogs.description: Intractable hiccups and elevated creatine kinase are often overlooked signs of severe hyponatremia. We explore the case of SIADH secondary to CNS inflammation, highlighting how metabolic complications like rhabdomyolysis can serve as vital clues to underlying electrolyte disturbances in neuroinflammatory conditions.

blogs.title: Colchicine for the Brain? Challenging Steroid Dogma in Neuro-Behçet's
blogs.description: Standard management for acute neuro-Behçet's typically involves high-dose corticosteroids and immunosuppressants. This post analyzes a rare case where colchicine monotherapy resolved neurological, mucocutaneous, and endocrine manifestations, questioning whether aggressive immunosuppression is always necessary in the acute phase.

blogs.title: The Concurrent Conundrum: Systemic and Neuro-Behçet's Diagnosed Simultaneously
blogs.description: Neurological involvement in Behçet's disease usually occurs years after the initial diagnosis. This post examines the rarity of concurrent presentation, discussing the diagnostic challenges and the importance of recognizing mucocutaneous features immediately upon CNS symptom onset rather than assuming a later neuro-BD timeline.

blogs.title: The Day 5 Ulcer: Why Serial Physical Exams Matter in Cryptic Autoimmune Disease
blogs.description: Diagnostic criteria for Behçet's disease were not met on admission but were confirmed days later when genital ulcers appeared. We discuss the value of serial physical examinations in patients with non-specific febrile illness, where delayed mucocutaneous findings can provide the definitive diagnosis for systemic autoimmune disease.

blogs.title: Fever, Headache, and Hyponatremia: Navigating the Diagnostic Maze in the ED
blogs.description: The triad of fever, headache, and hyponatremia presents a complex differential ranging from infection to malignancy to autoimmune etiologies. This post outlines a stepwise approach to workup, emphasizing when to pursue autoimmune panels versus infectious etiologies and how to avoid over-testing while ruling out critical mimics.
